title: Establish the contradiction

title: Establish the contradiction

title: Establish the contradiction

title: Show how scale could work

title: Show how scale could work
say: Some of those costs exist before the next customer uses a single gigabyte. Adding customers and traffic can spread the costs more widely—until capacity needs expanding again.

say: And capacity depends on another resource, one you can't see from the street: spectrum.

title: Unpack the spectrum headline
say: Spectrum is the range of radio frequencies a network uses to carry signals.

title: Unpack the spectrum headline
say: But different bands do different jobs. Higher frequencies can provide substantial capacity over shorter distances. Lower frequencies generally travel farther and penetrate buildings better.

title: Unpack the spectrum headline
say: Now look inside Jio's spectrum total.

title: Unpack the spectrum headline
say: About eighty-two percent of the aggregated bandwidth in these figures is in the twenty-six-gigahertz band. Airtel owns substantial bandwidth there too.

title: Unpack the spectrum headline
say: That band is useful. Its large contribution also explains why a single total cannot describe every aspect of network strength.

title: Unpack the spectrum headline
say: One distinctive Jio asset is its nationwide seven-hundred-megahertz holding, supporting wider reach and indoor coverage.

title: Unpack the spectrum headline
say: The advantage depends on the mix, geography and deployment—not just the largest number.

title: Unpack the spectrum headline
say: But even a well-equipped network faces a very ordinary question: will the customer keep paying?

title: The customers who leave

title: The customers who leave

title: What a price rise reveals
say: When tariffs rose, Jio's average revenue per user increased. But churn also rose, and subscriber growth slowed before recovering.

title: What a price rise reveals
say: That's why a higher revenue-per-user figure needs a second chart beside it.

title: What a price rise reveals

title: What a price rise reveals
say: A company has stronger pricing power when it can keep more of the benefit after departures, costs and competitive responses.

title: What a price rise reveals
say: For Jio, the evidence here is mixed. Higher revenue is encouraging. The customer response still matters.

say: And it takes more than Jio's own network to reach those customers. Follow the distribution and infrastructure relationships, and another part of the business comes into view.

title: The relationships underneath the network
say: Reliance Retail distributes Jio's prepaid connectivity. Large parts of the tower and fibre network involve other companies under long-term arrangements.

title: The relationships underneath the network
say: Those relationships can help a network expand efficiently. They also make contract terms important.

title: The relationships underneath the network
say: Who sets the price? What service is promised? What happens when an agreement changes or expires?

title: The relationships underneath the network
say: We don't have enough detail here to judge every arrangement. The point is that reach depends partly on relationships, not only on assets inside one company.

title: The relationships underneath the network
say: Now step back. Jio has scale, useful spectrum and encouraging retention. There is a serious case that these advantages could produce better results as the investment cycle changes.

title: The strongest positive case
say: This chart shows cash capital expenditure as a share of revenue: roughly forty-nine percent, falling to twenty-three percent over two years.

title: The strongest positive case
say: A network requires substantial investment before it earns its full potential. If an existing network can support more paying customers without equally large new spending, cash generation can improve.

title: The strongest positive case
say: That's the strongest positive case for Jio: scale and retention, followed by a less demanding phase of investment.

title: The strongest positive case
say: But lower spending in one period doesn't mean investment is finished. And it doesn't mean every earlier bill has been paid.

say: It helps support a business with enormous scale, distinctive spectrum assets and encouraging retention. Those are real reasons to take Jio seriously.

title: Return to the recharge
say: But scale becomes a durable financial advantage only when it produces better economics after the costs of maintaining, expanding and financing the network.

title: Return to the recharge
say: Our assessment is a narrow moat: some protection, with important questions about pricing power, comparable costs and returns on the capital invested.

title: Return to the recharge
say: The next evidence to watch is straightforward. Can Jio earn more per customer, keep its retention advantage, and turn that combination into stronger cash generation and capital returns?
